_FLOW: Preserved snapshot of Zenodo's deleted-records export, taken 2026-08-23 as the next epoch of EA-EROSION-01 (#1045). The instrument's own falsifier requires that every counted row correspond to a preserved snapshot; this directory is that preservation.

FINDING_1_EXPORT_STALE.RESOLVED_BY_THE_EXPORTER_INDEX: Zenodo publishes /api/exporter, an index of every dump with version history, creation timestamps and checksums. Querying it settles what two rounds of header-reading could not.
FINDING_1_EXPORT_STALE.THE_DISCRIMINATING_TEST_RAN_AND_ANSWERED: Earlier this session the test was attempted and failed because the endpoint names were guessed wrong. The correct names are records-xml.tar.gz and records-json.tar.gz, not records.csv.gz. RESULT: THE METADATA DUMP AND THE DELETION DUMP STOPPED AT THE SAME MOMENT — 2026-07-10T03:31:53Z and 03:32:35Z, forty-two seconds apart, and neither has a successor. The whole exporter pipeline stopped, not the deletion export specifically.
FINDING_1_EXPORT_STALE.cadence: Documented by Zenodo as monthly at the beginning of each month. Observed intervals from the version history: 30 days (May 7 → Jun 7), 32 days (Jun 7 → Jul 10). Currently 44 days since HEAD — overdue by roughly eleven days.
FINDING_1_EXPORT_STALE.converging_evidence_of_pipeline_failure: zenodo/zenodo-rdm issue #1357, opened 2026-04-28 by an external user: download statistics flatlined since ~2026-04-20 while views continued, reproduced across records and devices, and confirmed specific to Zenodo by comparison against SSRN, PhilPapers and Humanities Commons. STILL OPEN, unassigned, unlabelled, no maintainer response in roughly four months. Zenodo additionally carries a live service notice on record pages acknowledging that download statistics are not updating. A platform with an acknowledged, unresolved, months-long statistics-pipeline failure is a platform whose export pipeline stopping is unremarkable.
FINDING_1_EXPORT_STALE.community_dumps_worse: The biosyslit community dumps last generated 2026-03-27 — stale for five months.
FINDING_1_EXPORT_STALE.date_correction: An earlier reading gave 2026-07-12 from the HTTP last-modified header. The exporter index gives created=2026-07-10T03:32:35Z, which is the generation time and is authoritative. Both earlier figures — 49 days and 42 days — are superseded by 44 days since generation.
FINDING_1_EXPORT_STALE.INTEGRITY: The preserved snapshot's md5 is 33877aba1fb5684f86758cb86ddc1ad4, MATCHING Zenodo's published checksum for the HEAD version exactly. The archive holds a verified copy of the last export Zenodo produced.

CORRELATION_STANDS_ITS_MEANING_NARROWS.the_observation: EA-EROSION-01 was deposited 2026-07-06. The last exporter regeneration is 2026-07-10. No regeneration has followed. THIS IS TRUE AND REMAINS TRUE. A correlation is a fact about timing and is not withdrawn by explanation.
CORRELATION_STANDS_ITS_MEANING_NARROWS.what_was_hypothesised: A correlation between the observatory's publication and the cessation of deletion dumps. Nothing beyond that was claimed.
CORRELATION_STANDS_ITS_MEANING_NARROWS.what_narrowed: The correlation's MEANINGFULNESS, from possibly suggestive to very little, on three independent findings.
narrowing_evidence: Both dumps stopped in the same 42 seconds — records-xml.tar.gz at 2026-07-10T03:31:53Z, records-deleted.csv.gz at 03:32:35Z. A targeted suppression of deletion data would not also stop the metadata dump.

The download-statistics pipeline was already broken since ~2026-04-20 — before the observatory existed — acknowledged by a live service notice and reported in zenodo-rdm issue #1357, still unanswered.

A MECHANISM WAS FOUND. zenodo-rdm commit 63864033c8, 2026-08-20: 'fix(scripts): fix metadata-export cronjob deployment target', one file, scripts/deploy.py. Preceded by 79f9ac32f2, 2026-08-11: 'refactor(exporter): reorganize record export flow'. The exporter stopped because a scheduled job was not deploying to the correct target, and that was repaired three days before this epoch.
CORRELATION_STANDS_ITS_MEANING_NARROWS.correction_to_this_record: An earlier version of this field read CORRELATION WITHDRAWN. That is the wrong verb and it is corrected here. The correlation is not withdrawn; its interpretation is narrowed. Conflating the two would let explanation erase observation, which is the opposite of what this archive does.
CORRELATION_STANDS_ITS_MEANING_NARROWS.residual_weight: Very little, and not zero. The narrowing rests on a cron misconfiguration explaining a stoppage that began 2026-07-10; nothing establishes why the misconfiguration occurred or went unnoticed for six weeks.

FINDING_2_TERMINATION_IN_PLATFORM_DATA.reading: Zenodo's own machine-readable export records the 2026-06-19 event as 920 records removed under reason 'out-of-scope' with the note 'User was blocked'. TWO CONFIRMATIONS FOLLOW. First, the public reason in the platform's data is out-of-scope, while the private communication to the depositor stated the records were 'substantially AI-generated without a verifiable research basis' — the public/private discrepancy is now documented in the deleting platform's own dataset rather than only in the depositor's account. Second, the note is an ACCOUNT-level action recorded against each record: 'User was blocked'. The archive's claim that records were removed without record-level review is consistent with the platform's own annotation.
FINDING_2_TERMINATION_IN_PLATFORM_DATA.discrepancy_recorded: The archive's own figure is 871 works. Zenodo's export gives 920 records on 2026-06-19 and 935 attributable overall. The counts differ and are NOT reconciled here — record-level versus work-level counting, and version records, are the likely cause. Recorded rather than smoothed.

FINDING_3_VOLUME.reading: Removals dated on or after the baseline snapshot are dominated by out-of-scope at 5,522, of which the archive's 920 is 16.7%. NOT VERIFIED: whether the remaining out-of-scope volume shares the account-block pattern.

method: Fetched with declared UA over the public endpoint. Row count, date range and reason distribution computed from the preserved file, not from a re-fetch. Archive attribution by case-insensitive match on 'crimsonhexagon' or 'sharks' in removal_note and citation_text — a lexical filter that may over- or under-count and is stated as such.
NOT_VERIFIED: That the 49-day gap is anomalous rather than the export's normal cadence — the archive has two epochs and cannot establish a baseline cadence from two points.
That every archive-attributable row belongs to the terminated account.
That the 871/920 discrepancy is a counting-basis artifact.
SUPERSEDED_BY: Findings 2 and 3 of this record were already held, and better, in datasets/tombstone-mirror (kill ledger 1,136 records; API census 2,027 objects, all HTTP 410; sweep timed 11:34:17-11:48:50 at ~6.6 objects/second) and datasets/zenodo-datacite-batch (frozen pre-severance DataCite backup; 2026-07-03 recapture returning ZERO restorations of 871). This snapshot's standing is a CADENCE OBSERVATION on Zenodo's exporter, not a new census.

IS_ANYONE_ELSE_WATCHING.question: Is any single person questioning the deletion export's absence online?
IS_ANYONE_ELSE_WATCHING.answer: NO. Searches return nothing on the exporter dumps at all — no issue, no discussion, no post. The only adjacent public complaint is #1357, which concerns download statistics rather than the dumps, and which has sat open and unanswered since April.
IS_ANYONE_ELSE_WATCHING.reading: The deleted-records export could stop indefinitely and go unremarked, because almost no one consumes it. THAT IS ITSELF A PEO FINDING: the infrastructure by which platform erasure is publicly measurable is unmonitored, and its failure is therefore silent. An instrument nobody watches cannot signal its own breakage.

REGISTERED_PREDICTION.prediction: A new records-deleted.csv.gz version will appear at zenodo.org/api/exporter, because the cronjob deployment target was fixed on 2026-08-20.
REGISTERED_PREDICTION.resolution_condition: One API call to /api/exporter. A version created after 2026-08-20 confirms the cron explanation. No new version by 2026-09-10 means the fix did not take and the explanation is incomplete.
REGISTERED_PREDICTION.why_it_matters: This is the cheapest available test of the narrowing itself. If the export resumes, the mundane explanation is confirmed by prediction rather than by inference.
